```luau
fx.particle("flame", pos, { velocity = vec3(0, 1, 0), speed = 0.5 })        -- a jet
fx.particle("firework", pos, { count = 40, spread = 2, speed = 0.05 })       -- a burst
```
Particles fade on their own. A beam that stays is drawn again every other
tick:
```luau
local beam = { from = vec3(0.5, 76, 0.5), to = vec3(0.5, 66, 0.5), color = colors.cyan }
local conn = time.on_tick(function(tick)
    if tick % 2 ~= 0 then return end
    local points = {}
    for i = 0, 7 do points[i + 1] = beam.from:lerp(beam.to, i / 7) end
    fx.particle("dust", points, { color = beam.color, size = 2 })
end)
tween(beam, { to = beam.to + vec3(4, 0, 0) }, { duration = 1 })   -- its fields are plain; set or tween them
conn:cancel()                                                     -- and it is gone
```

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.markdown:
- `casino.*` covers everything under `casino`. `*` covers everything.
- A leading `-` takes a node away.
- The most specific node wins. Between two equally specific nodes, the `-`
wins.
The pack’s `citadel.yml` defines groups. Every player is in `default`.
```yaml
permissions:
  default: { nodes: [casino.play] }
  vip:     { inherits: [default], nodes: [casino.vip] }
  staff:   { inherits: [vip], nodes: [minecraft.command.gamemode, "casino.*", "-casino.debug"] }
```
The script puts players in groups:
- Groups last until the player leaves. Store them and re-add them in
`players.on_join`.
- Server operators (`operators:` in the server’s `citadel.yml`) have every
node.
- Gate your own commands with `player:has`.
- Same-name groups in two packs merge.
- The server stops on a group that inherits an undefined group, or on a
group named `operator`.

players.title: Players
players.markdown:
player
survival: nil on a game version that has no such rule
`player:give`, `player:take`, `player:inventory` and `player:count` work on
inventory stacks.
- A given stack merges into existing stacks, hotbar first.
- What does not fit is dropped from the give, not duplicated.
- Clicks in the player’s own window work as in the game, all seven click
modes included.
- A pack’s own menu over the inventory is `player.ui.menu{}` (see “Menus”).
- A chest’s stacks are `world.container` (see “containers”).
## Who sees whom
A player sees others in their room who are in view. Two settings remove a
player’s body from a client:
```luau
player.visible = false        -- from everyone; true or nil brings it back
viewer:hide(player)           -- from this viewer only; viewer:show(player) undoes it
viewer:can_see(player)        -- what the two add up to

-- a lobby where nobody sees anyone
room.players.on_join(function(p) p.visible = false end)
room.players.on_leave(function(p) p.visible = true end)

-- teams: each side sees only its own
for _, a in players.list() do
    for _, b in players.list() do
        if a.data.team ~= b.data.team then a:hide(b) else a:show(b) end
    end
end
```
- A hidden player is gone from that client: no body, name, armour or hitbox.
The `invisibility` effect differs: it shows armour and the held item.
- The tab list still shows hidden players.
- Both settings last across rooms.
- `hide` is by account, so it lasts when the other player rejoins.
- A new session resets both: nothing hidden, and `visible` is true.
## Health, food and `nil`
`player.health`, `player.max_health`, `player.food` and `player.saturation`
are `nil`, not `0`, on a game version with no rule for them. Every Alpha node
is one (a0.1.0 has no food and no damage). Across the engine, what a version
lacks is absent, not zero.
`health` is always the health of one individual now. `max_health` is always
the most it can be. This is the same for a player, for an entity in the world
and for a kind (a kind has `max_health` only).
- `player.max_health = n` takes 1 to 1024. `nil` gives the game’s own (20)
back. Another type or a number out of range is an error. It is an error on
a version with no damage rules.
- A lower maximum takes `player.health` down to it. A higher maximum does not
heal.
- `player.health = n` with `n` above the maximum gives the maximum. Food,
regeneration and peaceful healing stop at the maximum. A respawn fills to
it.
- Every Java client (1.7 to 26.3) draws the hearts of the maximum. A Bedrock
client draws no health today.
- The maximum lasts for the session, also across rooms and deaths. Set it in
`players.on_join`.
`cause` in `players.on_death` is one of `fall`, `drown`, `suffocate`, `void`,
`lava`, `fire`, `cactus`, `starve`, `attack` (a mob’s or a player’s hit),
`shot` (an arrow), `blast`, `magic` and `other` (a pack’s own
`player:damage`). `message` is the broadcast English death line. `by` is the
player who hit or shot them, or `nil`.
**A player is one value while connected.** Every event passes the same
`player`:
- `a == b` compares players, and a player can be a table key.
- `player.data` holds your own state. You need no table keyed by name.
- In `players.on_leave`, `player.name` and `player.data` still read. `data`
is kept for 10 seconds after they leave; after that a value you still hold
reads an empty table.
- `data` may name the player (`p.data.state = { player = p }`, a function
that uses `p`); it is let go with them all the same.
- A player who rejoins is a new value with empty `data`.
```luau
players.on_join(function(p) p.data.coins = 0 end)
players.on_leave(function(p) storage.set("coins." .. p.uuid, p.data.coins) end)
```

room-rules.title: Room rules
room-rules.markdown:
A `mode: full` server has them all on. A pack can turn one off.
A rule is `true` or `false`. A rule that you leave out keeps its value, and
so does a rule you write as `nil`. Any other value is an error:
`world.rules{ fall = 0 }` and `world.rules{ fall = "off" }` stop the script.
`redstone` is on in every room until a pack turns it off. With it off, no
signal moves: a lever lights no wire, a piston stays in, a pack block’s
`power` gives nothing and `block.powered` reads `false`. What was lit when
the rule changed stays as it is until something beside it changes.
`anticheat` checks what each Java player’s client claims:
- A player who flies, runs too fast, sends moves faster than the game ticks, or walks through full blocks goes back to the last legal position.
- A claim to stand on nothing does not prevent fall damage.
- A hit on something the player does not look at, or faster than 20 per second, does not land.
- After enough failed checks in a short time, the engine removes the player. The message names the check.
- The flight check skips creative and spectator players, a player who may fly (`player.can_fly`), a rider and a dead player.
- `player:push` and a movement effect (`speed`, `jump_boost`, `levitation`, `slow_falling`, `dolphins_grace`) exempt the player while they last. `player:teleport` is always allowed.
- A pack that moves players in any other way turns `anticheat` off: `world.rules{ anticheat = false }`.
`survival` gives the room to the engine’s survival, as on a `mode: full`
server:
- A broken block drops its normal drops.
- A block the world breaks by itself drops them too: a torch whose wall is
gone, a leaf that decays, a block an explosion or a piston breaks, sand
that cannot land.
- Placing uses up the stack.
- The inventory and a crafting table craft.
- A death drops the inventory, and the respawn button works.
- The engine saves the player’s inventory.
- It also turns on `fall`, `damage`, `hunger`, `anticheat` and `day_cycle`.
Without `survival`, a dig reaches no block, and a block the world breaks by
itself leaves no item. `game.block(name).drops = true` switches one block of
the game back on (see “Blocks”). A pack block still leaves the drops its
definition lists; `drops = "table"` is the game’s own drop and leaves
nothing. A survival pack puts `world.rules{ survival = true }` at the top,
and runs the same on either kind of server.
Anything that is not a rule is the pack’s job: `player:damage` for a hit,
`player.health` to heal, `players.on_death` and `players.on_respawn` for what
happens next, and `hit.player` in `players.on_click` for one player hitting
another:
```luau
world.rules{ fall = true }
players.on_click(function(player, hit)
    if hit.button == "left" and hit.player then
        hit.player:damage(2)
        hit.player:push(player:look() * 0.5 + vec3(0, 0.3, 0))
    end
end)
```

rooms.title: Rooms
rooms.markdown:
```luau
local room = rooms.create{
    spawn_point = vec3(0.5, 65, 0.5),
    generate = function(chunk) chunk:fill(chunk.min, chunk.min + vec3(15, 0, 15), "stone") end,
}
player:move_to(room)          -- the client swaps worlds in place
room.ui.title{ title = "Welcome" }
room:message("A new round starts")   -- a chat line to everyone in this room
room.players.on_join(function(p) end)  -- fires after move_to as well
print(player.room == room)    -- rooms compare by identity; `player.room` is nil while moving
room:destroy()                -- when the last player left; players still in it keep the world
```
- The global `players.on_join` fires on connect, in the main room. A room’s
own fires on each move in. `players.on_leave` matches.
## Spawn points
`spawn_point` is the position where a player arrives. `spawn` is never a
position: it is the call `world.spawn` and the switch of an entity kind.
- `citadel.yml` has `spawn_point: [x, y, z]` for the main room.
`rooms.create { spawn_point = vec3(..) }` sets it for a new room.
- A write to `world.spawn_point` or `room.spawn_point` changes where a player
arrives: on a join, on a respawn, and on a move to the room. The clients in
the room get the new compass target.
- The write is not stored. After a restart the room has the point of
`citadel.yml` or of the stored world again.
- The write does not move the chunks that stay loaded, the spawn protection,
or the area where no mob spawns by itself. Those stay at the first point.
- `player.spawn_point` is the player’s own respawn point. A bed sets the same
value where the game has beds. A point that a pack sets needs no bed. The
engine keeps the block of the position: `vec3(20.2, 65, -7.9)` reads back as
`vec3(20.5, 65, -7.5)`.
- `player.spawn_point = nil` also removes a point that a bed set.
- Manifest keys and `rooms.create` options are checked: an unknown key is
an error naming the field and the accepted keys.

scoreboard-with-a-button.title: Scoreboard with a button
scoreboard-with-a-button.markdown:
```luau
-- main.luau
world.on_generate(function(chunk)
    chunk:fill(vec3(chunk.min.x, 64, chunk.min.z), vec3(chunk.max.x, 64, chunk.max.z), "stone")
end)

local board = world.screen{ at = vec3(-2, 68, -10), facing = "south", width = 4, height = 2 }

local function redraw()
    board:clear(colors.black)
    board:text(16, 12, "TAPS", colors.yellow, 40)
    local y = 64
    for _, p in players.list() do
        local score = storage.get("taps." .. p.name) or 0
        board:text(16, y, p.name, colors.white, 28)
        board:text(board.width - 16 - board:measure(tostring(score), 28), y, tostring(score), colors.cyan, 28)
        y += 34
    end
end

players.on_join(function(player)
    player:hotbar{ [1] = { item = "lapis_block", name = "Tap me" } }
    player:message("Right click the block in your hand.", colors.cyan)
    redraw()
end)

players.on_leave(function()
    redraw()
end)

players.on_click(function(player, hit)
    if hit.slot ~= 1 or hit.button ~= "right" then
        return
    end
    local key = "taps." .. player.name
    storage.set(key, (storage.get(key) or 0) + 1)
    sound.play("block.note_block.hat", { at = player.at, pitch = 1.5 })
    redraw()
end)
```

screens.title: Screens
screens.markdown:
- Put it in the air blocks in front of a wall.
- `at` is the top-left frame as the viewer sees it.
- `facing` is the side the viewer stands on.
- Changes go out once per tick, as each frame’s box of changed pixels.
- Colours snap to the map palette (about 250 tones). Each client gets its
closest tone.
- `color.nearest(c)` does that snap in advance.
- Text is DejaVu Sans Bold, anti-aliased, 16 pixels by default. It has every
Latin letter, digits, symbols and `♠ ♥ ♦ ♣`.
- A screen belongs to its room and ends with the script.
- Players who join later see the current picture.
Set `on_click` (in `world.screen{}` or later) to get the pixel a player
clicks:
```luau
board.on_click = function(player, x, y, button)   -- button "left" or "right"
    board:circle(x, y, 6, colors.red)
end
board.on_click = nil   -- no hook again; false does the same
```
- A click on a block or the air behind the picture also counts.
- `players.on_click` still gets the click, with the frame’s `entity_id` and
no handle.
`board:view(player)` is one player’s own layer over the screen, with the same
drawing calls.
- Only that player receives it.
- See-through pixels show the shared picture. A new view is all
see-through, and `view:clear()` paints see-through.
- The call returns the same view until `view:destroy()` or the player leaves
the room.
- Canvases have views too.
`glow = true` makes glow frames on 1.17 and later, plain frames before. A
glow frame stays bright in a dark room.
Drawing notes:
- `line`, `ring` and `polygon` take fractional positions and blend into the
pixels under them. Draw them on a background, not on `colors.transparent`.
- A polygon point is `{x, y}` or `{ x = .., y = .. }`.
- Each `sprite` string is a row. Each character is a dot `scale` pixels
square (1 by default). A character with no colour (the `.` above) leaves
its pixels unchanged.
For a floor or a table, set `facing = "up"`, in the air blocks on top.
- `up` is the way the top of the picture points, `"north"` by default. Use
`"south"` for a player north of the table.
- Rows run away from `up`. With `up = "south"`, x runs west and y runs
north.
- Clients before 1.13 see nothing of a floor screen.
```luau
local felt = world.screen{ at = vec3(2, 66, 2), facing = "up", up = "south", width = 5, height = 3 }
```

server-settings.title: Server settings
server-settings.markdown:
```yaml
# citadel.yml
mode: lite              # "full" = Citadel plays the game, "lite" = the packs are the game
packs: packs            # where the packs are, relative to this folder
bind:                   # what to listen on; each line left out is this default
  java: 0.0.0.0:25565
  packs: 0.0.0.0:25566  # resource packs over HTTP; give a second server on one machine its own
  bedrock: 0.0.0.0:19132    # Bedrock over RakNet (UDP); "" turns it off
  nethernet: 0.0.0.0:19132  # Bedrock over NetherNet (TCP signaling, the same number as RakNet on UDP); "" turns it off
game: a0.1.0            # the game version, "1.8.9" (the default) or "a0.1.0"
world_dir: worlds/a0    # the world folder; a world keeps the game it was written by
operators:              # players with every permission, by uuid (Minefort writes the owner here)
  - 069a79f4-44e9-4726-a5be-fca90e38aaf5
online_mode: true       # check each player with Mojang, as vanilla does; this is the default
nethernet_tls:          # the certificate for Bedrock clients that dial HTTPS; not used behind a proxy with a forwarding secret
  cert: fullchain.pem
  key: privkey.pem
store_dir: data/store   # where `stores` keeps its files when no platform store was named; this is the default
```
A player’s identity comes from one of three places:
- Behind a proxy with `MODERN_FORWARDING_SECRET`: the proxy signs it.
- No proxy, `online_mode: true`: Citadel checks with Mojang.
- `online_mode: false`: nobody is checked, and the log warns at start.
Anyone can join with any name, an operator’s too.
Every key is optional, and so is the file. With no `packs` key, a `packs`
folder beside the world is used when one exists. An unknown key or mode
stops the server.
The mode is decided in this order:
1. a `--full` or `--lite` flag
2. this file
3. what the packs agree on in their own manifests
4. survival, when there are no packs.
## World
`world` says where a chunk comes from.
- `world = "script"`: `world.on_generate` makes the chunks. A chunk it does
not fill is air.
- `world = "overworld"`: Citadel’s terrain, with biomes, hills, caves, ores,
trees and sea level 63. Scripts only add to it (`world.on_populate`).
`seed` pins the map.
- `world = "hub"`: any other name is a world folder in the pack,
`<pack>/hub`, made once from a build or a vanilla world. The server reads
it chunk by chunk and saves player changes into it. A chunk the folder
lacks comes from `world.on_generate`, or is air.
`citadel import builds/lobby.schem <pack>/hub --at -186,48,-236 --spawn 0.5,65,0.5
`
Generate a map too big to make live into that folder ahead of time, with
the pack’s `world.on_generate`:
`citadel generate <pack> --from -4096,-6144 --to 4095,6143 # block corners; --threads n
`
It runs one script per core, and any map size fits in memory. Chunks
already in the folder are kept, so a stopped run continues.
`parts.define` declares a named part whose generator runs on request.
Build mode edits the folder by hand (see “Named parts”).
`citadel generate <pack> --part tower-3 # one part's generator, into the folder
citadel parts <pack> # every part: clean, modified, kept or orphaned, and who edited it
`
- **no `world` key**: the scripts are asked first. A chunk no script filled
is overworld terrain on a full server and air on a lite server.
**Chunks nobody is near are unloaded.** Every ten seconds the server drops
chunks beyond the view distance of all players and entities. When someone
returns, a stored world loads the chunk from disk (a changed chunk waits for
its save). A `script` world calls `on_generate` again.
So **`on_generate` must make the same blocks every time**. Draw from a hash
of the position, never `math.random`. A script-world chunk changed live
(`world.set_block`, `world.fill`) stays in memory.
**Where the world is.** A full server keeps its world in `world/`, beside
the server’s `citadel.yml`, with or without packs: the world is the
server’s, and a pack that is removed does not take the map with it. A lite
server keeps it in the first pack, `<pack>/data/world`. A dimension is a
folder beside the main world (`world_dungeon`). `world_dir` in the server’s
`citadel.yml` names another place.
The world’s `level.json` keeps the seed, spawn, time and weather of the first
run. Changing `seed` does nothing to an existing world. Delete the world
folder for a new map.
With no `spawn_point`, a `world: overworld` pack takes the first grass block above
sea level, ring by ring out from (0, 0). It searches once and stores the
result in `level.json`. With no `world` key, the spawn is the origin.
The chunks around the spawn are generated before the port opens.
## Terrain
`terrain` sets the overworld’s step list. Only `game: a0.1.0` has one.
Without `terrain`, the world uses the original game’s steps.
```yaml
game: a0.1.0
world: overworld
terrain:
  snow: true              # Alpha's snowy world: a frozen sea, snow on every open column
  steps:                  # the whole populate list, in order, in place of the jar's
    - { step: dungeons, count: 8 }
    - { step: clay, block: clay, size: 32, count: 10 }
    - { step: ore, block: coal_ore, size: 16, count: 20, below: 128 }
    - { step: ore, block: diamond_ore, size: 7, count: 4, below: 16 }   # four times the jar's
    - { step: trees, bonus: 10, big: 10 }
    - { step: patch, block: dandelion, count: 2 }
    - { step: patch, block: poppy, count: 1, chance: 2 }
    - { step: reeds, count: 10 }
    - { step: cactus, count: 1 }
    - { step: springs, fluid: water, count: 50, bound: 120, nesting: 1 }
    - { step: springs, fluid: lava, count: 20, bound: 112, nesting: 2 }
    - { step: snow }
```
| step | what it places |
| --- | --- |
| `dungeons` | `count` tries at a cobblestone room with a spawner and up to two chests |
| `clay` | `count` blobs of `block`, `size` long, into sand that starts under water |
| `ore` | `count` veins of `block`, `size` long, into stone below y `below` |
| `trees` | trees on the surface; one chunk in `bonus` gets one more, one in `big` grows big trees |
| `patch` | a patch of 64 tries at `block` — `count` times, or with `chance: n` one time in n |
| `reeds` | `count` clumps of sugar cane beside water |
| `cactus` | `count` clumps of cactus on sand |
| `springs` | `count` fluid sources in stone walls; `nesting` pushes them deeper |
| `snow` | a snow layer on every open column — in a `snow: true` world only |
`game.terrain` prints the original list. Start an edit from it.
- Order matters: moving or removing a step changes everything after it.
- A block must be one the game can name.
- A size or a bound must be at least 1.
- An unknown key stops the server.
- The list is stored in `level.json`. Like `seed`, a later edit changes
nothing for an existing world.
- `terrain` on a 1.8.9 world stops the server.

shared-stores.title: Shared stores
shared-stores.markdown:
On Minefort, a development workload and all instances of its experience share one store. A pack cannot choose another store. When `CITADEL_STORE` names a socket, that socket must work or the call fails.
**Without a socket, data lives in files that survive a restart.** Every local run works this way.
- Facts are in `data/store/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000.json`.
- A blob is a file under `data/store/blobs/<player-uuid>/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/`.
- Writes are atomic. A killed server keeps the previous value.
- `store_dir` in `citadel.yml` moves that directory. Two servers on one laptop need two directories.
- The first call logs which store opened, and where.
```luau
local scores = stores.open()
players.on_join(function(player)
    local visits = scores:increment("visits", 1)
    player:message("Visit number " .. tostring(visits))
end)
```
Every call yields while the I/O runs. Other callbacks continue.
- Call from scripts, callbacks or tasks. Do not call from synchronous ask handlers or at module initialization.
- A pack can have up to 32 pending requests.
- The `storage` API stays a local per-pack JSON file, even in a published world.
The calls:
- `stores.open()` returns the experience’s store. Passing an id is an error.
- `handle:get(key)` returns `(value, version)`. Version zero means absent.
- `handle:set(key, value, if_version, lease?)` returns the new version.
- `handle:delete(key, if_version, lease?)` removes a value.
- `handle:increment(key, by)` atomically increments a number, starting at zero.
- `handle:list(prefix?, cursor?, limit?)` returns `(keys, next_cursor)`.
- `handle:blob_get(player_uuid, key)` returns `(binary_string_or_nil, version)`.
- `handle:blob_put(player_uuid, key, bytes, if_version, lease?)` returns the new version.
- `handle:blob_delete(player_uuid, key, if_version, lease?)` deletes a blob.
- `stores.blob_list(player_uuid)` returns entries across all blob stores in this scope.
- `stores.lease(key, holder, ttl_ms)` returns a fencing token.
- `stores.renew(key, token)` and `stores.release(key, token)` maintain a lease.
Facts and blobs have separate keys: a fact `"world"` and a blob `"world"` are different values.
Limits:
- Keys: at most 256 bytes. Facts: at most 1 MiB. Blobs: at most 32 MiB.
- Hosted storage per experience: 512 MiB, and 1 MiB more for every Java player who has ever joined it. There is no limit on how many values. Each player may have at most 1,000 blobs.
- 100,000 issued lease tokens. Leases last up to one hour.
- Hosted blobs are not in world archive backups.
`pcall` preserves the value passed to `error`, including tables, numbers and
booleans. Native binding errors remain readable strings. Store errors reach
`pcall` as a table:
- A version conflict is `{err="conflict", version=current_version}`.
- A stale fencing token is `{err="held", by=current_holder}`.

shop.title: Shop
shop.markdown:
**The player says yes or no in Minefort’s own dialog, not in the pack.** The pack learns only whether a purchase was paid. It never sees the player’s Gems, the price or a reason.
```luau
players.on_join(function(player)
    if shop.owns(player, "vip") then
        player:message("Welcome back, VIP")
    else
        shop.prompt(player, "vip") -- Minefort shows its dialog
    end
end)

shop.on_paid(function(purchase)
    -- Hand the item over here. Returning without an error marks it delivered.
    for _, player in players.list() do
        if player.uuid == purchase.player then player:message("Thanks for buying VIP") end
    end
end)

shop.on_declined(function(purchase)
    -- The player said no, or did not answer. Close the pack's own shop screen.
end)
```
- `shop.prompt(player, product)` returns a request id, or nil when Minefort did not offer it. A player or a uuid string.
- `shop.owns(player, product)` returns whether the player owns a pass.
- `shop.on_paid(fn)` calls `fn({request, player, product})` for each undelivered paid purchase. It runs on the server the player is on: an experience has many servers, and each one hands over only to its own players. A purchase for a player who is not online waits until they join one. At least one active paid handler must complete successfully, and all active paid handlers must succeed, before the purchase is acknowledged. With no paid handler, or if one raises an error, it stays pending. An `on_declined` listener alone never acknowledges a paid purchase. Delivery can repeat after a failure or restart; use `purchase.request` as a durable idempotency key when granting a reward.
- `shop.on_declined(fn)` calls `fn({request, player, product})` when the player said no or did not answer.
- A product key is 1 to 32 characters of `a-z`, `0-9`, `_` and `-`. Another key is an error.
Calls yield, like `stores`. Only experiences in the Minefort Creator Rewards Program have the shop. Elsewhere, and in local runs, `prompt` returns nil and `owns` returns false.
After an error, read again. After an I/O timeout, a write may have committed. Retry only versioned writes, never an increment. A world release rollback does not rewind shared facts or blobs.

sound.title: Sound
sound.markdown:
## sound.stream
`sound.stream` plays a live stream or a pack’s sound file through the
players’ voice mods, with no screen. A live stream is MP3, as a radio station
sends it, or the sound of an FLV stream. A file is OGG (Vorbis), MP3 or WAV in
the pack; it is decoded while it plays, never loaded whole.
```luau
-- 3D: from speakers. Each player hears every speaker within `distance`.
local radio = sound.stream{ url = "https://radio.example.org/live.mp3", at = vec3(10, 67, 28), distance = 24 }
local pa = sound.stream{ url = url, at = { vec3(10, 67, 28), vec3(-10, 67, 28), captain }, distance = 16 }
local hum = sound.stream{ file = "assets/music/engine.ogg", at = engine_room, loop = true }

-- No place: the same volume for each listener, no fade, no direction.
sound.stream{ url = url }                         -- everyone in the room
sound.stream{ file = "assets/voice/welcome.mp3", to = player }
sound.stream{ url = url, to = { p1, p2 }, name = "Radio" }

radio.playing            -- false once stopped, or once a file that does not loop ends
pa:move(2, vec3(-12, 67, 30))   -- speakers are numbered from 1
pa:add(npc)                     -- a speaker that follows a player or an entity; gives its number
pa:remove(3)
radio:listen(player)            -- starts to hear it
radio:unlisten(player)          -- stops hearing it
radio:stop()
```
- Give `url` or `file`, never both. `loop = true` is for a file only: a live
stream has no end, and if it drops it is tried again every 2 seconds.
- `at` is a vec3, a player, an entity, or a list of them. A speaker that
follows a player or entity moves with it, and is silent while they are
gone. `at = {}` starts with no speakers; `add` gives it some.
- All speakers play the same sound at the same time, as a speaker system
does. A player hears every speaker in range, each from its own place, and
the voice mod mixes them. Each one is a packet of its own to that player:
three speakers in range send three times the sound’s data.
- `distance` is 1 to 128 blocks, 48 when not given. It needs `at`: a sound
with no place has no distance, and giving one is an error.
- `to` is a player or a list of players. Without it, everyone in the room
hears the sound, players who join later too. `listen` and `unlisten`
change who hears while it plays.
- `name` (1 to 16 characters, `"Sounds"` when not given) is the sound’s own
volume slider in the mod.
- `move`, `add` and `remove` on a sound with no `at` are an error. On a
stopped sound, every call does nothing.
- The sound stops with `stop()`, or when the script stops or reloads.
- Players hear it through Simple Voice Chat, as a screen’s stream: a player
without the mod, or on a client older than 1.13, hears nothing.
|  | `sound.play` | `sound.stream` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| How it reaches the player | The game’s or the pack’s resource pack; the client plays it | Simple Voice Chat, from the server |
| Mod needed | No | Yes |
| Control | Start and stop | Speakers, moving sources, a list of listeners, all players in time |
| Best for | Short effects: a click, a door, an alarm | Music, ambience, long voice lines, radios, speaker systems |

storage.title: Storage
storage.markdown:
`storage.status()` returns `{ pending: boolean, error: string? }`. A write
failure remains visible and is retried. `storage.flush()` yields until the
current values are saved, or raises the write error. Call it from a callback
or `task.spawn`, after initialization. `storage.set` changes memory immediately;
unflushed changes can still be lost if the process crashes.
Strings and record keys in JSON-backed storage must be valid UTF-8; invalid
bytes raise an error instead of being replaced. Use `stores.open():blob_put` for
binary data. The UTF-8 rule also applies to persistent entity and block data
and other JSON-backed APIs.
A value it cannot hold is an error that names it, never a changed copy:
```luau
local t = { 1, 2 }; t.total = 3
storage.set("score", t)
-- error names score and total: mixed lists and records have no JSON shape.

storage.set("tick", function() end)
-- error: storage cannot save tick: a function is not a JSON value...
```
- Records use string keys; lists must be contiguous from index 1. A table cannot mix the two.
- Numbers must be finite, and cyclic tables raise an error before changing stored data.
- Persistent data views are accepted directly; reads return detached plain tables.
- Only `nil` deletes. `{}` saves and reads back as an empty table.

text-formatting.title: Text formatting
text-formatting.markdown:
Text is a string or a table:
```luau
"Lap 2/3"                                                   -- words, in the surface's own colour
{ "1st", color = colors.gold, bold = true }                 -- one styled run
{ "Lap ", { "2", color = "white", bold = true }, "/3", color = "gray" }
player.ui.sidebar{ title = { "KART", color = "gold", bold = true }, lines = {
    { { "1. ", color = "yellow" }, "Mario" },
    { "2. Luigi", color = color(0.4, 1, 0.4) },
} }
```
- A table’s entries are its **runs**: strings or tables.
- Its named fields style all its runs: `color`, `bold`, `italic`,
`underline`, `strike`. A run’s own style wins.
- A call’s own colour (`player:message(text, color)`, `ui.actionbar(text, color)`, a title’s `color`, a text display’s `color`, `npc:say(text, color)`) colours the words with no colour.
- Any other field is an error that names the five style fields.
- A live text field (`bar.title`, a display’s `text`) reads back the words.
## Text that moves
A text table’s `effect` styles **every letter**. A whole text can also be a
**function of the time**.
- The sidebar, boss bars, the tab list and text displays recompute them ten
times a second. Other surfaces show the frame at send time.
- Only what moves is recomputed: a sidebar’s still lines are read when it is
set. To change one, set the sidebar again.
- A moving text table shown to many players at once, such as one title
table every player’s sidebar uses, is worked out once a frame.
```luau
-- a rainbow, one cycle a second: letter, its number i of n, and t = time.now()
local rainbow = function(letter, i, n, t) return { color = color.hsv((i - 1) / n + t, 1, 1) } end
p.ui.sidebar { title = { "KART", effect = rainbow, bold = true } }

local sparkle = function(letter, i, n, t)
    if (i + math.floor(t * 8)) % 4 == 0 then
        return { color = "white", bold = true }
    end
    return { color = "gold" }                -- or nil: the letter as it was
end
world.display { kind = "text", at = vec3(0.5, 70, 0.5), text = { "WINNER", effect = sparkle } }

-- a text that is a function of the time: rebuilt every frame
ui.sidebar { title = "Lobby", lines = {
    function(t) return { "Next race in " .. math.max(0, math.ceil(race_at - t)), color = "yellow" } end,
} }
```
- An effect returns a style (`color`, `bold`, `italic`, `underline`,
`strike`, plus `text` to replace the letter, `""` to hide it) or `nil`.
- More effects, each one line:
`-- colours across the letters, flowing at `speed` cycles a second
function(_, i, n, t) return { color = color.gradient(list, (i - 1) / n - t * speed, true) } end
-- the whole text in one colour at a time, `speed` times through the list a second
function(_, _, _, t) return { color = list[math.floor(t * speed * #list) % #list + 1] } end
-- the letters appear one after another, `rate` a second from `from = time.now()`
function(_, i, _, t) if i > (t - from) * rate then return { text = "" } end end
`
- An effect or text function that errors keeps its last frame and logs why.
Clients from 1.16 get exact colours, older ones the nearest of the sixteen.
Sidebar lines take hex colours from 1.20.3.
A screen or canvas draws text as pixels, in the colour of its `text` call.

time-and-tweens.title: Time and tweens
time-and-tweens.markdown:
`time.now()` starts again at zero when the pack does. Use it for what
happens while the pack runs: a race, a cooldown. For something that ends
after a restart, such as a rental of a week, keep an `os.time()` in
`stores` and compare with it. It is UTC, so every server of an
experience reads the same clock, whatever its region:
```luau
local s = stores.open()
local ends, version = s:get("rent:" .. player.uuid)
if not ends or os.time() >= ends then          -- over, even if no server ran meanwhile
    s:set("rent:" .. player.uuid, os.time() + 7 * 24 * 3600, version)
end
```
## Tween
`tween` eases a live number, `vec3`, `color` or `rotation` field, once a tick, such as
a display’s `at` or a player’s `speed`.
`easing` is `"linear"` (the default), `"in"`, `"out"`, `"in_out"` or
`"bounce"`. A `duration` that is not a number, or an `easing` that is not
one of these names, is an error. A display’s own `animate` tweens on the client: smoother, but
1.19.4 and later only. Use `tween` for everything else and every client.

vectors-and-colours.title: Vectors and colours
vectors-and-colours.markdown:
```luau
local a = vec3(1, 2, 3)
a + b, a - b, -a, a * 2, a * b, a / 2, a == b
a:magnitude(), a:unit(), a:dot(b), a:cross(b), a:distance(b), a:lerp(b, t), a:floor(), a:with{ y = 70 }
vec3.zero, vec3.up

local c = color(1, 0, 0.5)   -- or colors.red, color.hsv(0.6, 1, 1)
c * 0.5, c * d, c:lerp(d, t), c == d
color.gradient({ "gold", colors.white, "#3366ff" }, u)   -- the colour u (0..1) of the way along the list
color.gradient(list, u, true)                           -- a loop: u wraps, and the last colour runs back into the first
color.nearest(c)             -- the colour a screen or canvas really shows, since a picture snaps to the map palette
```

version-info.title: Version info
version-info.markdown:
`citadel.version` is the engine build (`0.1.0`).
`citadel.env` is:
- `"development"` on the Minefort workload where an experience is built.
- `"unlisted"` or `"published"` on an experience’s instances, by visibility.
- `"published"` on a Minefort server that is not an experience.
- `"development"` anywhere else.
Gate debug tools on it:
```luau
if citadel.env == "development" then
    -- builder-only commands, verbose logs, …
end
```
Build mode (`/build`, `/part`; see “Named parts”) exists on `"development"` only.

your-first-pack.title: Your first pack
your-first-pack.markdown:
## 1. Create the pack
Make a folder named `first` and put this `citadel.yml` inside it:
```yaml
# citadel.yml
name: first
entry: main.luau
motd: My first Citadel pack
spawn_point: [0.5, 65.0, 0.5]
gamemode: 2
mode: lite
world: script
```
`entry` names the script to run. `world: script` means that script supplies
the terrain, and `mode: lite` makes your pack the game. Adventure mode
(`gamemode: 2`) lets players explore without breaking the floor.
`spawn_point` places their feet one block above the floor, in the centre
of the gold marker you will create next.
## 2. Add the script
Create `main.luau` beside `citadel.yml`:
```luau
--!strict
-- A small lobby: solid ground, a welcome, and a way back to spawn.

world.on_generate(function(chunk)
    chunk:fill(
        vec3(chunk.min.x, 64, chunk.min.z),
        vec3(chunk.max.x, 64, chunk.max.z),
        "stone"
    )
    chunk:set(vec3(0, 64, 0), "gold_block")
end)

players.on_join(function(player)
    player.ui.title{
        title = "Welcome",
        subtitle = player.name,
        color = "aqua",
    }
    player:message("Walk around, then type /spawn to return to the gold block.", "aqua")
end)

commands.add("spawn", function(player)
    player:teleport(world.spawn_point)
    player:message("You are back at spawn.", "green")
end, { help = "Return to the lobby spawn" })
```
Read the three callbacks in order:
- `world.on_generate` fills each chunk with a stone floor at y = 64, then
marks `(0, 64, 0)` with gold. `chunk:set` ignores positions outside its
chunk. `vec3(x, y, z)` describes a position; y is height.
- `players.on_join` receives the player who joined. The title and message
go to that player. Register the callback once; Citadel calls it when
needed.
- `commands.add` registers `spawn` without a slash. When a player types
`/spawn`, `player:teleport(world.spawn_point)` returns them to the point
from the manifest. Reading it avoids repeating the coordinates.
## 3. Run it and check your work
With `citadel` on your `PATH`, run this from the directory containing `first`:
```sh
citadel --lite --pack ./first
```
Keep the server running and join `localhost:25565` from Minecraft Java
Edition, or use the address and port configured for your server. You should
see a welcome and stand on the gold block. Walk away, type `/spawn`, and
check that you return to it with a confirmation in chat.
## 4. Make an edit
Change `title = "Welcome"` to `title = "My lobby"` and save. Citadel reloads
`.luau` files while players stay connected, and runs the join callback for
those players again. The new title should appear. If it does not, check
the server log for a script error.
Reloading keeps existing chunks: edits to `world.on_generate` affect newly
generated terrain. Restart after editing `citadel.yml`. As a next exercise,
add a `/hello` command that sends a message to the player who uses it.

zones-and-raycasts.title: Zones and raycasts
zones-and-raycasts.markdown:
```luau
local goal = world.zone{ from = vec3(10, 64, 10), to = vec3(14, 66, 14),
    on_enter = function(player) message(player.name .. " scored", colors.lime) end,
    on_leave = function(player) end }
goal:contains(player)                -- boolean
goal:players()                       -- who is in it now
goal:destroy()

players.near(pos, 8)                 -- every player within eight blocks of a point
players.within(from, to)             -- every player inside a box of blocks, corners included

world.raycast(from, direction, 32)   -- the first block a ray meets within 32 blocks, or nil:
--   { block = vec3, face = "up" | "down" | "north" | "south" | "west" | "east" }
world.raycast(player.at + vec3(0, 1.62, 0), player:look())   -- what the player is looking at

world.sees(from, to)                 -- true when no block stops the line between the two points
world.raycasts(rays, out, n)         -- n lines at once, in buffers; see below
local block, sky, open = world.light_at(pos)   -- block light 0..15, sky light 0..15, open sky
world.path(from, to, { size = { 0.6, 1.95 } })  -- the points a body walks, a list of vec3, or nil
```
- `world.sees` and `world.raycasts` look as a mob looks: a block with a
collision box stops the line, glass and leaves too. Water, lava, grass and
flowers do not.
- `world.raycasts(rays, out, n)`: `rays` is a buffer with six f64 for each
line: from x, y, z, then to x, y, z. `out` gets one f64 for each line: how
far from `from` the first block is that stops it, or -1 when the line is
clear. One call for all the bodies of an `on_think` is much cheaper than one
call each.
- `world.light_at(pos)` gives three values: the block light, the sky light,
and `true` when no block above stops the sky.
- `world.path(from, to, opts)` is the game’s own search for a mob: four ways
from each block, a step up of one block, a fall of at most `fall` blocks. It
gives the middle of each block to walk on, from `from` to the block at `to`.
The options: `size` (a number, or `{ width, height }`; 0.6 by 1.8),
`swim = true` to go through water, `fall` (3), `range` (how far it may go
from the goal; the distance plus 16), `budget` (the most blocks it looks at;
2000). A search that stops early gives the part that came closest. `nil`
when it found no step at all.
- A path costs the pack, not the tick. A short one costs some microseconds; a
long one around a big wall costs more. Ask for a new one when the old one is
old, not each think.
- `from` and `to` are block positions, in either order. Both corners are
inside.
- A player is inside when their feet are.
- Disconnecting inside a zone runs `on_leave`.
- A zone ends with the script.

AskCount.title: AskCount type
AskCount.lead: What one kind of ask has cost this pack, and what every kind has together. An ask is a question the engine puts to a pack with a deadline on it; an answer that does not arrive in time is not used.

members.name: asks
members.description: Questions the engine put to this pack.

members.name: answered
members.description: Answers that arrived in time.

members.name: missed
members.description: Deadlines that passed with no answer.

members.name: late
members.description: Answers that arrived after the engine had acted, and were dropped.

members.name: skipped
members.description: Asks never sent, because this kind is switched off for this pack.

members.name: disabled
members.description: True once the engine has stopped asking this pack this kind at all.

Asks.title: Asks type
Asks.lead: What the engine's questions with a deadline have cost this pack, in total and per kind: `citadel.budget().asks`.

members.name: kinds
members.description: The same counters per kind of question, e.g. `kinds["break"].missed`.

Bar.title: Bar type
Bar.lead: A boss bar, from `ui.bossbar` for the room or `player.ui.bossbar` for one player; title, progress and colour are live.

members.name: destroy
members.description: Removes the bar.

members.name: title
members.description: Reads back the words; takes any text.

members.name: progress
members.description: How full the bar is, 0 to 1; live.

members.name: color
members.description: The bar's colour, from its own closed set; anything else is white. Live.

members.name: visible
members.description: Whether players see the bar; false takes it off their screens, true or nil shows it again.

BarColor.title: BarColor type
BarColor.lead: A boss bar's colour is its own closed set — six the client draws, and anything else is white. It is not an `Ink`: the bar has no hex form.

Billboard.title: Billboard type
Billboard.lead: How a display turns toward the viewer: "fixed" never turns, "vertical" turns about the up axis, "horizontal" tips up and down, "center" does both.

BiomeDefinition.title: BiomeDefinition type
BiomeDefinition.lead: What a pack changes about the vanilla biome its own biome copies. Each colour is a `Color` or a colour name such as "#7fd8c8".

members.name: name
members.description: Lower case letters, digits and underscores. The pack's name goes in front: "crystal" becomes "mypack:crystal".

members.name: like
members.description: The vanilla biome to copy; "plains" when left out.

members.name: water_fog
members.description: The colour of the view under water.

members.name: fog
members.description: The colour of the far distance.

Biomes.title: Biomes type
Biomes.lead: The biomes a pack adds to the game.

members.name: define
members.description: Defines a biome, or changes the one of that name, and returns its full name ("mypack:crystal"). Call it at the top of the script: a player learns the biomes when they join.

Block.title: Block type
Block.lead: One block the game version has, in its own numbers, from `game.block(name)`: hardness, light, fire and material.

members.name: name
members.description: The block's canonical name.

members.name: behaviour
members.description: The rule Citadel runs for it, such as "grass", "flowing", "torch" or "falling"; nil for a block that does nothing on its own.

members.name: hardness
members.description: Seconds-scale hardness in this version's numbers; below zero is unbreakable.

members.name: random_ticks
members.description: Whether the random-tick pass acts on it.

members.name: opaque
members.description: Whether it is an opaque full cube, which is not the material's question.

members.name: light
members.description: What it gives off, 0..15, and what a step through it takes away.

members.name: light_filter
members.description: What a step through it takes off the light, 0 to 15.

members.name: resistance
members.description: The three the block-update tables own: nil in a game that has none.

members.name: flammability
members.description: Fire's two numbers: how readily it catches and how fast it burns away. Nil in a game with no block-update tables.

members.name: material
members.description: The jar's Material as five questions; nil in a game with no block-update tables.

members.name: drops
members.description: The one field a pack writes. Whether a block of this kind that the world breaks by itself leaves its item: true leaves it on a lite world too, false never, nil is the world's default. Reads what this pack set.

BlockAmendSpec.title: BlockAmendSpec type
BlockAmendSpec.lead: What `game.blocks.amend` takes: **hooks only**.  Every tnt in every world already looks like tnt and is as hard as tnt, so a data column here is refused by name. For a block of your own with different numbers, `game.blocks.define { extends = "tnt" }`.

members.name: on_use
members.signature: blockAmendSpec.on_use((block: BlockAt, player: Player ?, held: string ?, base: (...any) -> any) -> Used ?) → ?
members.description: Somebody right-clicked it; `held` is the item in hand. Answers "used" or "pass"; a missed deadline passes the click through.

members.name: on_break
members.signature: blockAmendSpec.on_break((block: BlockAt, player: Player ?, by: Breaker, base: (...any) -> any) -> Drops ?) → ?
members.description: Something broke it; `by` says what. Answers "none", "table" or a drops list.

members.name: on_step
members.signature: blockAmendSpec.on_step((block: BlockAt, body: Body, base: (...any) -> any) -> ()) → ?
members.description: A body (a player, mob, item or other) is standing on it.

members.name: on_tick
members.description: A scheduled tick this block asked for came due.

members.name: on_random_tick
members.description: The random pass landed on it.

members.name: on_place
members.signature: blockAmendSpec.on_place((block: BlockAt, player: Player ?, base: (...any) -> any) -> ()) → ?
members.description: A player put it down.

members.name: on_neighbour
members.signature: blockAmendSpec.on_neighbour((block: BlockAt, from: Vec3, announced: string, base: (...any) -> any) -> ()) → ?
members.description: A neighbour at `from` changed; `announced` is the block the notifier announced itself as.

members.name: on_trigger
members.signature: blockAmendSpec.on_trigger((block: BlockAt, cause: Trigger, base: (...any) -> any) -> ()) → ?
members.description: It was lit, blasted or burnt; `cause` is "ignite", "explosion" or "fire".

members.name: on_power
members.signature: blockAmendSpec.on_power((block: BlockAt, powered: boolean, base: (...any) -> any) -> ()) → ?
members.description: A redstone signal started (`powered` is true) or stopped reaching it. Called once for each, not for every change beside it.

members.name: on_added
members.description: It has just been stored, whatever stored it.

members.name: on_removed
members.description: It has just gone.

BlockAt.title: BlockAt type
BlockAt.lead: The block a hook was called about.  Reads are fields and acts are methods. The reads are **live** — the world as it is right now — and everything that changes the world is carried out by the engine the moment the hook returns, in the order it was asked for.

members.name: get
members.description: The block one face away, by name; nil where that chunk is not in memory.

members.name: set
members.description: Puts another block at this position.

members.name: destroy
members.description: Takes it out, leaving nothing.

members.name: become
members.description: **The door**: this block stops being a block, and that entity appears.

members.name: drop
members.description: A name, or an item table: a pack item keeps its id.

members.name: schedule
members.description: Asks for this block's `on_tick`, `tick_every` seconds from now.

members.name: notify
members.description: Tells the six neighbours this block changed.

members.name: data
members.description: What this block remembers beyond its state; kept with the position, saved with the chunk, and gone when the block goes. Nested writes are tracked; whole-record assignment is supported. Copy before keeping it beyond the hook.

members.name: at
members.description: The block's position; a live read.

members.name: name
members.description: The block's name with its namespace, such as "rave:crate"; a live read.

members.name: room
members.description: Which room the block is in.

members.name: state
members.description: Which of this definition's states it is in, counting from 1. Writable, and bounds-checked against the definition's own `looks` list: it *is* the block state, so a crop's stages cost nothing.

members.name: facing
members.description: A facing block's front: "north", "south", "west", "east"; nil otherwise. Writable.

members.name: powered
members.description: Whether a redstone signal reaches it: what a lamp asks. A live read; nil where the chunk is not loaded.

BlockDef.title: BlockDef type
BlockDef.lead: The handle `define` hands back. Equality is identity — two handles are the same block when they name the same block.

members.name: name
members.description: Canonical, with the pack's namespace already on it: "rave:crate".

members.name: states
members.description: How many states it has; `block.state` counts 1 to this.

members.name: item
members.description: The block as an item, when the definition gave it one: `player:give(def.item)`.

BlockPick.title: BlockPick type
BlockPick.lead: One block, or one of a list chosen by a field: `floor(by)` counts through the list and starts again at its end.

BlockRef.title: BlockRef type
BlockRef.lead: A block, as anything that takes one will take it.

BlockSpec.title: BlockSpec type
BlockSpec.lead: What a definition says a block *is*.  Every hook takes `base` as its **last** argument: call it and you extended what is under you, leave it out and you replaced it. `base` is a decision rather than a reentrant call — its effects land when your hook returns, and calling it twice happens once.

members.name: on_use
members.signature: blockSpec.on_use((block: BlockAt, player: Player ?, held: string ?, base: (...any) -> any) -> Used ?) → ?
members.description: The hooks. Writing one is what asks for it — there is no flag beside `on_random_tick` saying the random pass may land here.

members.name: on_break
members.signature: blockSpec.on_break((block: BlockAt, player: Player ?, by: Breaker, base: (...any) -> any) -> Drops ?) → ?
members.description: Something broke it. Answers "none", "table" or a drops list; fails closed to the definition's `drops`.

members.name: on_step
members.signature: blockSpec.on_step((block: BlockAt, body: Body, base: (...any) -> any) -> ()) → ?
members.description: A body is standing on it; `body` is `{ id, kind }`.

members.name: on_tick
members.description: A scheduled tick this block asked for came due.

members.name: on_random_tick
members.description: The random pass landed on it. Not the same thing as `on_tick`, which is why it has the longer name.

members.name: on_place
members.signature: blockSpec.on_place((block: BlockAt, player: Player ?, base: (...any) -> any) -> ()) → ?
members.description: A player put it down; `block.data` is empty then, ready to be filled.

members.name: on_neighbour
members.signature: blockSpec.on_neighbour((block: BlockAt, from: Vec3, announced: string, base: (...any) -> any) -> ()) → ?
members.description: A neighbour changed; `from` is its position and `announced` the block name the notifier announced itself as.

members.name: on_trigger
members.signature: blockSpec.on_trigger((block: BlockAt, cause: Trigger, base: (...any) -> any) -> ()) → ?
members.description: It was lit, blasted or burnt; `cause` is "ignite", "explosion" or "fire".

members.name: on_power
members.signature: blockSpec.on_power((block: BlockAt, powered: boolean, base: (...any) -> any) -> ()) → ?
members.description: A redstone signal started (`powered` is true) or stopped reaching it. Called once for each, not for every change beside it.

members.name: on_added
members.description: It has just been stored, whatever stored it.

members.name: on_removed
members.description: It has just gone from the world.

members.name: name
members.description: Without a namespace. The pack's own is put in front of it, and a colon here is refused: a pack cannot write another pack's name.

members.name: looks
members.description: A block state the client already draws, because a client has never heard of this pack. One name, or one per state in state order. `|` takes the first this version has: "crimson_planks|nether_brick".

members.name: hardness
members.description: Seconds-scale, as vanilla's hardness is; below zero is unbreakable.

members.name: resistance
members.description: What an explosion has to chew through.

members.name: material
members.signature: blockSpec.material: { solid: boolean ?, covers: boolean ?, firm: boolean ?, liquid: boolean ?, burns: boolean ?, }?
members.description: The jar's Material as five questions: solid, covers (grass under it dies), firm (snow and ice need it), liquid, burns.

members.name: opacity
members.description: What a step through it takes off the light; 15 is an opaque cube.

members.name: light
members.description: What it gives off, 0 to 15.

members.name: tick_every
members.description: Seconds between `block:schedule()` and `on_tick`; 0.5 unless you say.

members.name: drops
members.description: What a break leaves — and, because `on_break` fails closed, what it leaves when this pack is too slow to answer. Never the looks block's. false is nothing, as "none" is.

members.name: item
members.description: The block in a hand. Its `id` is set to the block's name, so placing it puts this block down, and a break leaves it unless `drops` says. false is no item, also for a block with a texture.

members.name: texture
members.description: Its own picture on 1.21.4+: one for every state, or one per state.

members.name: model
members.description: Its own shape on 1.21.4+, in place of `texture`: a model that stays inside the block, one for every state or one per state. The block collides as its `looks` block does: "rail" is walked through.

members.name: facing
members.description: Turns its front to whoever places it; `block.facing` reads and turns it.

members.name: power
members.description: What it gives a redstone circuit, 0 or 15: one number for every face, a table keyed by face (the names `texture` takes), or a list of either with one entry per state. It is the power a block of redstone gives.

members.name: label
members.description: The name of the item a textured block comes with.

members.name: extends
members.description: A handle, a game block's name, a plain table of fields and hooks, or a list of those **innermost first**. There is no class and no metatable: fields merge and hooks wrap.

Blocks.title: Blocks type
Blocks.lead: `game.blocks`: defines a pack's own blocks and amends the game's own, at load time.

members.name: define
members.description: Load-time only: a world may already be holding blocks of a definition, so one that arrived later would change the rules under the players standing on it. Define at the top of `main.luau`.

members.name: amend
members.description: Only the game's own blocks, never another pack's.

Body.title: Body type
Body.lead: Whatever is standing on one. `kind` is `"mob"` for a cow or a zombie.

BodyRotation.title: BodyRotation type
BodyRotation.lead: Degrees: 0 yaw faces south, 90 west; positive pitch tips down. Constructors default missing angles to zero; later writes preserve them.
BodyRotation.typedef: { read yaw: number?, read pitch: number? }

Breaker.title: Breaker type
Breaker.lead: What took a block out, and with what.

members.name: cause
members.description: What took the block out: a player, fire, an explosion, flowing water, or the loss of what held it up ("support").

members.name: tool
members.description: The item in hand, or nil for a bare hand and for the four causes that have none.

members.name: creative
members.description: Whether a creative player broke it; creative takes the block and leaves nothing. False for the four causes with no player.

Budget.title: Budget type
Budget.lead: What a pack's tick and event callbacks are allowed per tick, together, and what it did with it. Milliseconds throughout.

members.name: of
members.description: `budget_ms` in citadel.yml; 2 by default.

members.name: used
members.description: What the last tick spent.

members.name: peak
members.description: The most any tick has spent.

members.name: skipped
members.description: Callbacks not run for want of budget, since the script started.

members.name: dropped
members.description: Ordinary events lost to queue overflow. Joins, leaves, deaths and respawns are retained with their original player sessions.

members.name: slowest
members.description: The slowest single callback so far, by short hook name.

members.name: asks
members.description: The engine's questions to this pack, and what it did with those.

Builder.title: Builder type
Builder.lead: What `world.build` hands the function it is given. Coordinates are whole blocks of the build's own and may be negative; later writes win.

members.name: block
members.description: Sets one block of the build; later writes win.

members.name: box
members.signature: builder:box(from: Vec3, to: Vec3, block: string)
members.description: Inclusive corners, in any order, like `chunk:fill`.

members.name: line
members.signature: builder:line(from: Vec3, to: Vec3, block: string)
members.description: Every block the straight line between the ends passes through.

members.name: part
members.description: What `fn` writes is a named part, found by `citadel render --part` and `citadel check` once pasted. Nested calls name "tower/roof".

Canvas.title: Canvas type
Canvas.lead: A picture of one or more maps with no frame of its own, from `world.canvas`, for a frame display, a hand or a screen.

members.name: view
members.description: The map id of its top-left map, for a `filled_map`. Returns that player's own layer over the canvas, drawn with the same calls; only they see it.

members.name: destroy
members.description: Removes the canvas; clients that saw it keep its last picture, and its id is never reused.

Chunk.title: Chunk type
Chunk.lead: A 16 by 16 column of blocks, handed to `world.on_generate`, `world.on_populate` and a room's `generate` to fill.

members.name: get
members.description: Chunk X coordinate (16 blocks each). Chunk Z coordinate (16 blocks each). The chunk's lowest corner, inclusive; y runs 0..255 or the game version's height. The chunk's highest corner, inclusive. Returns the block there now, by name; air outside the chunk.

members.name: set
members.description: Sets one block; positions outside the chunk are ignored.

members.name: fill
members.signature: chunk:fill(from: Vec3, to: Vec3, block: string)
members.description: Fills a box of blocks, clipped to the chunk.

members.name: paste
members.signature: chunk:paste(schem: Schematic, origin: Vec3, opts: { air: boolean ?, part: string ? }?)
members.description: Clipped to this chunk; air is skipped unless `air` is true. `part` names the paste for `citadel render --part` and `citadel check`; the build's own `b:part`s are then inside it ("house/roof").

members.name: get_biome
members.description: Returns the biome of the column at `pos`, by name; `nil` outside the chunk. A biome belongs to a column, so `pos.y` is not read.

members.name: set_biome
members.description: Sets the biome of one column: a vanilla name ("desert") or the name `game.biomes.define` returned.

members.name: fill_biome
members.signature: chunk:fill_biome(from: Vec3, to: Vec3, biome: string)
members.description: Sets the biome of every column in a box, clipped to the chunk.

ColorName.title: ColorName type
ColorName.lead: Every colour's name: Minecraft's sixteen, which every client has had since 1.7, six more, and "transparent". `colors` holds the same names.

Command.title: Command type
Command.lead: A command a pack added, from `commands.add`; change its suggestions or `cancel` it.

members.name: suggest
members.signature: command:suggest(arg: string, words: ({ Suggestion } | Suggester | false)?)
members.description: What `arg` offers from now on: a list, a function, or nil or false for nothing.

members.name: cancel
members.description: Takes the command away.

CommandOpts.title: CommandOpts type
CommandOpts.lead: The options of `commands.add`: a permission node, aliases, the /help line and suggestions per argument.

members.name: permission
members.description: A permission node; without it the command is not shown and not run.

members.name: aliases
members.description: More names for the same command: { "hub", "lobby" }.

members.name: help
members.description: The line /help shows after the usage.

members.name: suggest
members.description: Per argument name: the words to offer, or a function that returns them.

Commands.title: commands global · type Commands
Commands.lead: Adds a room's slash commands from a usage line: the `commands` global, or `room.commands`.

members.name: add
members.signature: commands.add(usage: string, fn: (player: Player, args: { [string]: any }) -> string ?, opts: CommandOpts ?) → Command
members.description: usage: "bet <amount:integer 1..10000> [color:red|black]". Types: word, integer, number (with an optional min..max), player, a|b|c, text... (the rest of the line as a string), words... (as a list). args holds each argument by name; an optional one not typed is nil. Return a string and the player reads it in red.

members.name: run
members.description: Runs a pack's command for player as if they typed it ("/servers"), with their permissions. false when no pack in their room declared it.

Connection.title: Connection type
Connection.lead: An event subscription or repeating timer; task functions return threads.

members.name: cancel
members.description: Stops the subscription or repeating timer, including from its own callback.

Container.title: Container type
Container.lead: A chest's stacks: `world.container(pos)`. A chest a player has open is theirs until it closes — `take` takes nothing, `put` puts nothing.

members.name: items
members.description: The filled slots, in order.

members.name: take
members.description: Up to `count` (1 unless you say) of what matches; how many it took.

members.name: put
members.description: How many did not fit; 0 when all of it went in.

members.name: size
members.description: How many slots the chest has, e.g. 27; 0 once it has gone.

members.name: at
members.description: The chest's block position.

Context.title: Context type
Context.lead: How an item display is posed; a read gives back the same words.

DamageHit.title: DamageHit type
DamageHit.lead: A hit on a player, before it lands: what `players.on_damage` hands a pack.

members.name: amount
members.description: Half hearts, before armour.

members.name: cause
members.description: "fall", "drown", "suffocate", "void", "lava", "fire", "cactus", "starve", "attack", "shot", "blast" or "magic".

members.name: by
members.description: The player who hit, or who shot the arrow.

members.name: kind
members.description: The kind's name ("Skeleton") when a mob did it.

DataView.title: DataView type
DataView.lead: An attached JSON record/list, with tracked nested writes and generalized iteration. Runtime userdata: use data.copy for ordinary table operations. Roots use string keys; nested lists use contiguous indices starting at 1. Assignment validates the entire value. Hook views expire after their callback batch finishes.

members.name: refresh
members.description: Whether the player still has it open. Draws a live view (a function) again.

members.name: update
members.description: A new view in place: a window, or a function that makes one.

members.name: destroy
members.description: Closes it.

DialogNode.title: DialogNode type
DialogNode.lead: A node of a dialog, made by `ui.kit`: a table with a `kind`.

Display.title: Display type
Display.lead: An item, text, block or frame shown in the world, from `world.display`; its place, rotation, scale and look are live.

members.name: animate
members.signature: display:animate(opts: { at: Vec3 ?, scale: (Vec3 | number)?, rotation: Orientation ?, text: Text ?, color: Ink ?, background: (Ink | false)?, line_width: number ?, shadow: boolean ?, duration: number ?, })
members.description: Makes one tweened change of place, scale, rotation or text over `duration` seconds (0.5 by default), played by the client.

members.name: move
members.description: Removes the display. Sets position and optional rotation together.

members.name: id
members.description: The raw entity id. `hit.entity` hands back this handle itself, so a pack rarely needs the number.

members.name: billboard
members.description: Whether it is still present. Read-only. Where it sits; live, every kind. Its yaw, pitch and roll in degrees; live. Pitch 90 lays a text flat on a table. Reads a vec3; write a number for every axis at once. How it turns toward the viewer; text defaults to "center", the other kinds to "fixed".

members.name: glow
members.description: Its outline colour; nil or false for none.

members.name: duration
members.description: Seconds later changes take to play out on the client (1.19.4 and later); 0 by default.

members.name: glide
members.description: Advanced movement smoothing in seconds (1.20.2+); default 0.1, 0 follows duration.

members.name: lead
members.description: Advanced: true enables linear prediction. Default false; nil restores it. Normally submit current positions and leave this alone.

members.name: item
members.description: item kind

members.name: canvas
members.description: Item kind: the canvas shown as a filled map; written as a canvas, read back as its map id.

members.name: context
members.description: Item kind: how the item is posed, as in a frame, a hand or on the ground.

members.name: text
members.description: text kind Reads back the words; takes any text.

members.name: color
members.description: The colour of the words that did not pick one.

members.name: background
members.description: Text kind: the colour behind the words; nil or false for none.

members.name: line_width
members.description: Text kind: the width its lines wrap at; 200 by default.

members.name: shadow
members.description: Text kind: whether the words have a shadow; false by default.

members.name: block
members.description: block kind

Drops.title: Drops type
Drops.lead: What a broken block leaves. "table" is whatever the site that broke it would have left — the version's drop table for a player's hands, a roll for a blast, nothing at all for a fire — and "none" is nothing, which is what a pack block leaves unless it says otherwise.

DurableStore.title: DurableStore type
DurableStore.lead: Shared durable stores. Calls yield; pcall catches structured errors such as {err = "conflict", version = 3}. One store per experience.

members.name: get
members.description: Returns a fact's value and its version; version 0 means absent.

members.name: set
members.signature: durableStore:set(key: string, value: any, if_version: number, lease: number ?) → number
members.description: Writes a fact if its version is still `if_version`, and returns the new version. A mismatch errors with {err = "conflict"}.

members.name: delete
members.signature: durableStore:delete(key: string, if_version: number, lease: number ?)
members.description: Removes a fact if its version is still `if_version`.

members.name: increment
members.description: Adds `by` to a number atomically, starting at zero, and returns the result. Never retry it blindly after a timeout.

members.name: list
members.signature: durableStore:list(prefix: string ?, cursor: string ?, limit: number ?) → ({string}, string ?)
members.description: Returns fact keys with this prefix and the cursor for the next page, or nil at the end.

members.name: blob_get
members.description: Returns one player's binary blob, or nil, and its version; `owner` is the player's uuid.

members.name: blob_put
members.signature: durableStore:blob_put(owner: string, key: string, bytes: string, if_version: number, lease: number ?) → number
members.description: Writes a player's binary blob if its version is still `if_version`, and returns the new version. At most 32 MiB.

members.name: blob_delete
members.signature: durableStore:blob_delete(owner: string, key: string, if_version: number, lease: number ?)
members.description: Deletes a player's blob if its version is still `if_version`.

Easing.title: Easing type
Easing.lead: How a tween moves over its duration: "linear" (the default) at one speed, "in" starts slow, "out" ends slow, "in_out" both, "bounce" bounces at the end.

Effect.title: Effect type
Effect.lead: A function called for every letter each frame a text shows, handing back how that letter looks; `i` of `n` is the letter's place, `t` is `time.now()`.
Effect.typedef: (letter: string, i: number, n: number, t: number) -> LetterStyle?

Entities.title: Entities type
Entities.lead: `game.entities`: the three verbs over one shape.

members.name: define
members.description: Load time only. A definition is a fact about the world.

members.name: amend
members.signature: entities.amend(name: string, hooks: EntityAmendSpec, options: EntityAmendOptions ?)
members.description: The game's own content only — never another pack's.

members.name: names
members.description: Every kind by name: the pack's own and the game's, mob or not. `mob = true` gives the mob kinds only, `mob = false` the rest.

EntityAmendOptions.title: EntityAmendOptions type
EntityAmendOptions.lead: A pack's hooks on one of the game's own entities. Hooks only: every pig already looks like a pig, so the data columns are refused by name.

members.name: on_spawn
members.description: Called when a new entity of this kind spawns; told, never waited on.

members.name: on_load
members.description: Called for an entity that already existed: a saved chunk loaded it, or a reload rebound it.

members.name: on_steer
members.description: Wrapped behavior runs first unless options.replace = true.

members.name: on_tick
members.description: Wrapped behavior runs first unless options.replace = true.

members.name: on_damage
members.description: Asked when it takes damage; return "ignore" to cancel it. Silence or a missed deadline is "take".

members.name: on_remove
members.description: Called when it leaves the world; `why` is "removed", "settled", "killed" or "unloaded". Not called when the pack goes away.

EntityDef.title: EntityDef type
EntityDef.lead: What `define{}` hands back. Usable anywhere the name is, so an author rarely types the namespace at all.
EntityDef.typedef: { read name: string, read mob: false }

EntityHandle.title: EntityHandle type
EntityHandle.lead: A body the world moves: a pack's own entity, a mob, a stack on the ground.  Every read is a fresh look at the world, so a handle to something that has died reads `nil`. Inside a hook the same handle reads the entity as it was at the top of the tick, and its writes land at that hook's own slot.

members.name: play
members.description: Model size: reads vec3; write a positive number or equal-axis vec3. Nil without a model. Plays a model entity's animation from the start; on the one already playing, `speed` only changes its speed.

members.name: stop
members.description: Stops a model entity's animation; the parts stay where they are.

members.name: move
members.description: Gone on the next tick. Sets position and optional rotation together.

members.name: push
members.description: A shove, in blocks a tick, added to what it is already doing.

members.name: settle
members.description: It stops being an entity and is a block again where it stands. No argument: the entity remembers what it was.

members.name: nearby
members.description: What else is around it, by horizontal distance.

members.name: id
members.description: Its entity id, the one players.on_click reports in `hit.entity_id`.

members.name: name
members.description: The kind's name: "cow", "rave:rocket". Nil once it is gone.

members.name: alive
members.description: Whether it is still in the world. A hook only runs for one that is.

members.name: age
members.description: Ticks lived.

members.name: velocity
members.description: Where it is, live; writing it is a teleport. Nil once it is gone. Partial writes preserve other angles; nil after removal. Bodies have no roll. How it is moving, live; writing it is steering by hand. Nil once it is gone. writing it is steering by hand

members.name: on_ground
members.description: Whether it stands on something. Nil once it is gone.

members.name: health
members.description: Its health now. Nil once it is gone.

members.name: max_health
members.description: The most health its kind gives it. Nil for an entity that is not a mob and once it is gone. Read-only.

members.name: hostile
members.description: Whether its kind is hostile. Nil once it is gone.

members.name: physics
members.description: Which order of operations moves it: "vehicle", "living", "falling", "item" or "none".

members.name: origin
members.description: The block it used to be, for anything that arrived through a transition; nil for anything that was never a block.

members.name: data
members.description: A pack-defined entity's attached record. Nested edits write through. Saved with persist = "save". Built-in entities raise an error on access. on_steer/on_tick views expire after the callback batch; copy to keep a snapshot.

members.name: forward
members.description: The intent fields: what a body *wants* to do, which is what steering is. Writing one outside `on_steer` lasts until the next decision.

members.name: strafe
members.description: Intent: 1 left, -1 right. A vehicle's seat 1 writes it from the keys every tick.

members.name: jumping
members.description: Intent: whether it wants to jump. A vehicle's seat 1 writes it from the keys every tick.

members.name: flying
members.description: Intent, a living body with can_fly only: true flies (no gravity; forward moves it along its look, pitch included), false falls and walks. Setting it true on another body is an error.

members.name: driver
members.description: Whether it is in water now. False for an entity that is not alive. The player supplying driving input from seat 1; nil for an NPC or empty seat.

members.name: paint
members.description: Every occupant by seat number, including NPCs; nil means empty. Material name to colour; write-only.

EntityKind.title: EntityKind type
EntityKind.lead: One kind the game version has, in its own numbers, from `game.entities.<kind>`: name, size, max_health, speed and drop. A kind that is not a mob (an arrow, a boat, primed TNT; `mob == false`) has `name`, `mob`, `width`, `height` and `physics` only: every other fact is nil for it, and a write to `spawn`, `attacks` or `interact` and a call of `amend` are errors.

members.name: amend
members.description: The same as `game.entities.amend(name, hooks)`.

members.name: name
members.description: Its modern registry name: "cow".

members.name: mob
members.description: Whether the kind is a mob: true for a cow, false for an arrow.

members.name: physics
members.description: For a kind that is not a mob, which order of operations moves it: "item", "falling", "vehicle" or "none". Nil for a mob kind.

members.name: behaviour
members.description: The name of the behaviour the engine runs for this kind, such as "sheep" or "living".

members.name: profile
members.description: Read-only copy; nil for a specialized behavior without a shared profile.

members.name: registry_name
members.description: This version's own registry spelling: "Cow". A dungeon spawner stores this one.

members.name: width
members.description: Its width in blocks, in this version's numbers.

members.name: height
members.description: Its height in blocks, in this version's numbers.

members.name: max_health
members.description: The most health one of this kind has, in this version's numbers. `health` on a kind is an error: health is what one entity has now.

members.name: speed
members.description: Blocks a tick at a full walk.

members.name: hostile
members.description: Whether it is hostile.

members.name: drop
members.description: The item its death leaves behind, such as "leather"; nil for none.

members.name: spawn
members.description: The one writable field. `true`: the kind is in this world as the game defines it: it spawns by the game's own rule, also on a `mode: lite` world, and `attacks` and `interact` are on for it unless a pack sets them; an error on a 1.8.9 world with no biomes, where nothing would spawn it. `false`: the kind never spawns by itself in this world; spawner blocks, `world.spawn`, `/summon` and breeding still make it. `nil`: the pack says nothing and the world's default applies: no natural spawning on a `mode: lite` world and in a room from `rooms.create`, the game's own rule on a `mode: full` world and after `world.rules{ survival = true }`. A table is an error today. Reads what this pack set (`true`, `false` or nil), not the game's own rule. The value is this room's (`room.game.entities.cow.spawn`) and this pack's: a `false` of any pack wins. Every write is an error on a game with no natural spawning (a0.1.0 to a0.1.3).

members.name: attacks
members.description: Whether its hits hurt players. `nil`: on for a kind with `spawn = true`, else the room's `damage` rule. The kind's own setting is stronger than the room's rule. It covers the kind's own hit, its arrow (also after the shooter died) and a creeper's blast. `false` stops the damage to players only: a blast still breaks blocks.

members.name: interact
members.description: Whether a player's right click on it has the game's effect (milk, a saddle). `nil`: on for a kind with `spawn = true`, else the room's `survival`. `true` is an error on 1.8.9, which has no right click on a mob.
